Subject: Redwood Private — egress/IP whitelist requirements (initial)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — BlueCrest's infra team asked for a concise list of outbound endpoints and IPs we need to allow for the Redwood Private control plane and private endpoints so we can get the firewall ticket moving. We also attached a network diagram and asked procurement to queue the security questionnaire.

What we need from you:
- Minimal set of destination IP ranges (or FQDNs and ports) used by Redwood components (control plane, telemetry, licensing callbacks)
- Whether connections are egress-only from customer VPC or mutual TLS inbound is expected
- A short risk matrix: what breaks if an outbound path is blocked (e.g., rollouts, logs, license checks)
- Any recommended NAT/proxy configuration for traffic inspection

Attachments: bluecrest_network_diagram.pdf

Can you get an initial matrix by next Wednesday (26 May)? Procurement copied to track timelines.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Cloud Ops — BlueCrest Financial

Subject: Re: Redwood Private — egress/IP whitelist requirements (initial)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and diagram. Taking this on.

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood Private control-plane callbacks are egress-only from customer network (outbound TLS to Redwood-managed endpoints). No public inbound ports are required for control-plane heartbeats.
- We can provide both a short list of stable FQDNs (for customers using egress allowlists) and a preferred set of static IP ranges for customers who require IP allowlisting at the firewall/NAT.
- Common failure modes if egress is blocked: model updates will fail, telemetry and usage billing will be delayed, canary rollouts fallback to local model variant (if configured), and license verification attempts may cause degraded UX.

I will assemble a permit matrix and coordinate with Mina on the port-level controls and with Marissa on the support/operational guidance. Expect the draft by Tuesday EOD (25 May). If you need the quick CSV earlier, I can push it tomorrow.

Regards,
Tessa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

--
Tessa Morgan
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood Private — egress/IP whitelist requirements (initial) — tech matrix draft

Tessa / team — draft attached (redwood-egress-permit-matrix.xlsx). Highlights:

Summary table (high level):
- Control plane (management):
  - Dest: control.redwood-infra.net (FQDN)
  - IP ranges: 34.192.10.0/24, 34.192.11.0/24 (stable for next 12 months)
  - Ports: 443 (TLS)
  - Protocol: HTTPS (TLS 1.3 preferred)
  - Required: Yes (if blocked: no model/version changes, dashboard metrics missing)

- Telemetry & usage (optional for air-gapped customers but recommended for billing):
  - Dest: telemetry.redwood-infra.net
  - IP ranges: 34.193.5.0/24
  - Ports: 443
  - Required: No (if blocked: usage logs buffered locally; reporting delayed)

- Model artifact sync (optional if you pre-push artifacts):
  - Dest: artifacts.redwood-infra.net / s3.redwood-infra.net
  - IP ranges: 3.210.88.0/24 (note: large object fetches use multiple ephemeral IPs; recommend allowing FQDN or NAT with proxy)
  - Ports: 443; 22 (only for admin rsync in special setups)

- License & entitlement checks:
  - Dest: license.redwood-infra.net
  - IP ranges: 34.194.7.0/24
  - Ports: 443
  - Required: periodic checks; if blocked, agents run in grace mode for 72 hours before manual recovery

Firewall / NAT guidance:
- Preferred pattern: egress to FQDNs over TLS with outbound inspection at TLS termination proxy (if your security practice disallows decryption, allowlist IP ranges at the edge NAT).
- For strict allowlist customers: deny-by-default, allow only the control-plane IP ranges and a small set for telemetry/artifacts. Provide a fallback by enabling local artifact snapshot to avoid runtime fetches.

Risk matrix (short):
- Block control plane -> rollout failures, no config updates
- Block license -> agents degraded after 72 hours
- Block artifacts -> cold-start failures for models not preseeded

Attachments: redwood-egress-permit-matrix.xlsx

Notes: IP ranges above are BGP-advertised from our edge and we’ll provide signed attestations for customers that require them. Jonas — adding the TLS fingerprint/CA bundle in the other doc.

-Mina
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Redwood Private — egress/IP whitelist requirements (initial) — TLS details and attestation

Sarah — following up on Mina's matrix. A few technical clarifications:

- TLS and CA info: all control-plane endpoints use mutual TLS for server authentication only (mTLS client certs are not required by default). We authenticate using our standard CA chain signed by Redwood Root CA (sha256:AB:CD:12:34...). We can provide the CA bundle and expected certificate fingerprints in a zip attachment.
- IP stability: we commit to a 30-day notice for any planned IP prefix changes that would affect the stable lists. Emergency changes may occur due to DDoS mitigation; in those cases we'll provide as much notice as possible and temporary alternate FQDNs.
- Monitoring/alerting hooks: we can expose a read-only status endpoint and provide a PagerDuty escalation path for control-plane incidents (incorporate into the SLA).

Attached: redwood-private-deploy-firewall-reqs.docx (contains the CA bundle reference and sample IPTables rules for on-prem appliances).

Cheers,
Jonas
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Sarah / procurement — thanks for the questions. Summary and next steps below: 

Deliverables we will provide by EOD Monday 31 May:
- Signed attestation PDF listing the stable IP ranges and the 30-day change policy
- A single-sheet "permit matrix" CSV that maps component -> FQDN -> IP ranges -> ports -> failure impact (suitable for firewall tickets)
- CA bundle + expected cert fingerprints (tar.gz) for validation by your TLS proxies
- Example IPTables/ASA rules and proxy config snippets for common enterprise setups

Operational notes for BlueCrest:
- If you must block artifacts fetches, please pre-stage model bundles into the private registry; otherwise expect degraded cold-start behavior.
- We recommend a NAT translation that preserves source IPs for our support traces; if that isn't possible, preserve a consistent egress IP range via a managed NAT gateway.

If procurement needs us to accept the 30-day clause, we can agree to it for planned changes. For emergency mitigations, we'll commit to an expedited notice + alternate FQDNs; we'll add the exact language into the security addendum.

I'll upload the deliverables to the Drive link and send the DocuSign redline back to procurement. Let me know if you'd like a short 30-minute call to walk the firewall team through the CSV.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
